text:
julia: heads-up — bringing up aether-18b (v1.0) on int4 for perf evals, hitting OOMs when we hit concurrent batches >5 and long outputs (>=200 tokens). sharing logs below and current config.

matt: can you paste the config you're testing with?

julia: sure — baseline:
```json
{
  "model": "aether-18b",
  "quant": "int4",
  "batch_size": 8,
  "max_new_tokens": 256,
  "prefetch_kv": true,
  "kv_eviction_threshold": 0.25
}
```

anita: odd — 8 + 256 seems high for int4 on the 48GB nodes. are you seeing fragmentation or pure allocation failures?

julia: a mix. logs show repeated failed allocations and later smaller OOMs after some requests succeed. snippet: 
```
[2024-02-12T14:03:22Z] alloc failed: cannot allocate 1.2G, fallback to evict
[2024-02-12T14:03:22Z] kv cache evicted 3 entries (approx 512MB)
[2024-02-12T14:03:24Z] alloc error: out of memory while reserving 384MB
```

kai: smells like memory fragmentation — int4 reduces per-layer memory but increases allocator churn due to many small temp buffers. Have you tried lowering batch_size or enabling a warmstart?

julia: tried batch_size 4 — much fewer OOMs but latency SLOs nosedive under load. warmstart (single dummy request per worker at spin-up) helps briefly but fragmentation returns after sustained traffic.

matt: two-pronged suggestion: 1) conservative defaults for this model in hosted catalog: batch_size: 4, max_new_tokens: 160; 2) server-side tuning: enable slab allocator defrag and bump `slot_reserve_mb` to 512 for this model variant.

anita: agree. also try toggling `kv_eviction_threshold` to 0.1 — keep more KV in cache and avoid frequent evictions that create alloc churn. but watch tail latency tradeoffs.

julia: testing now with:
```yaml
batch_size: 4
max_new_tokens: 160
slot_reserve_mb: 512
kv_eviction_threshold: 0.1
warmstart_probe: true
```

deploy-bot: rollout started: aether-18b v1.0 int4 safety-net config -> staging (canary 10%)

julia: early canary results: no OOMs in 30m, p95 latency +18% vs baseline int8, throughput -22%. Quality regressions minimal on our eval set (perplexity +0.9).

kai: those latency/hit numbers are expected. next: run an A/B with int8 quant at same batch settings to confirm perf/quality tradeoffs. also schedule a longer soak (6h) to surface fragmentation over time.

matt: if soak surfaces fragmentation again, we should consider an on-host periodic defrag job that triggers during low traffic or implement an allocator that coalesces free ranges. file a follow-up runbook item either way.

anita: logging note — add a KV-churn metric to console so we can correlate evictions with OOM windows.

julia: added. will post full soak logs and evaluation metrics in ~8h. thanks all :thumbsup:
